findings.reason: the author must cite where the census was run or restate the requirement as unquantified, otherwise a worker implements a channel for a population it cannot identify or recount.
findings.text: §8 states "The second benchmark round also found 44 derived parents whose case files show none of their children and 15 members with no producer in the graph", but neither figure occurs in any committed second-round artifact: grep over docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/* returns 0 files matching "children" against a positive control of 22 files matching "incumbent", and benchmark-second-round-incumbent-defects.json carries only the held-out defect classes — so the two counts behind the children-channel and no-producer requirements cannot be traced or reproduced

findings.reason: the node's central action is a text change, and where it lands decides the section's write scope; an unresolved answer sends the worker to guess on the lead's catalog.
findings.text: §9 requires "a flagged inconsistency is repaired once, changing only the flagged field of the flagged members" and reports "those repaired", while its closing sentence says "No stored text changes until the lead has read the 20-family comparison"; no route says where a repair lives between the two, so a dispatched node must either write the live catalog (forbidden by the last clause) or produce repairs it cannot report as made

findings.reason: without one partition the section's population and its per-family denominators are undefined, so its acceptance measure has no fixed base.
findings.text: §9 defines a family as "the members of one parent, and the members that differ by one grammar segment such as component, species, position or operator"; the two groupings are different partitions, so the set of families the pass runs over and the member counts the evidence reports per family cannot be reconciled

findings.reason: the plan needs either an edge making §3 depend on §8, or a statement that a prompt change invalidates the ruling and the held-out round is rescored.
findings.text: the depends-on map (plan.html:20) leaves §3 free to dispatch now (it waits only on the done §1 and §2) and gives §8 no edge to it, yet §8's done-when permits changing any stage's prompt text "to receive a channel the census shows it was missing" and §3 owns prompt tuning ("the case file or the prompt is changed in answer to the previous round's failures") — so §3's ruling can be made on a prompt §8 then changes, and §6 regenerates with a prompt the benchmark never scored

findings.reason: the plan's own cost discipline puts a ceiling on every model-calling section, and §8 is the widest census in the plan.
findings.text: §8 calls a model for every pipeline stage over the equilibrium group and the 87 held-out members (295 names across seven stages) and states no spend ceiling, while every other implementing section states spend beside a ceiling (§3 USD 25, §6 USD 30, §7 USD 10); a node can therefore incur an unbounded metered cost with nothing to compare it against

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited evidence paths exist, extensionless hrefs resolve as .html, and "the definitions plan" in §9 resolves to docs/plans/sn-definitions-by-construction.html.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9's done-when (plan.html:61) defines "family" two incompatible ways, so the population its per-family counts are taken over is undefined; §8's done-when is measurable and carries both a withheld-channel negative control and a positive control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8 and §9 both name docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/ for their records, the paths exist, and §7's two cited JSON files resolve there.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new sections carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8 attributes a 44/15 census result to the second benchmark round, and no committed second-round artifact contains either figure; the section's stated context root cause (the §2 case file imported by nothing) is verified true.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8's clauses all serve the one goal of recording and counting what each stage was given, and each other node names one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the depends-on map (plan.html:20) lets §8 change any stage's prompt text while §3, already dispatchable, rules the structure and model on the prompts as they stand, and nothing makes §3 wait for §8 or re-check the ruling after a prompt change.
